results.title: Trump family member reveals major trauma at age 2 that 'would scar him for life'
results.description: Donald Trump's niece says the president's lifelong cruelty can be traced to a frightening year when he was a toddler. That year, she says, left him alone with a father she calls a "sociopath." Mary Trump, who holds a doctorate in clinical psychology, made the case in a new post on her Substack newsletter, The Good in Us. It's a follow-up to her Thanksgiving Day post about the mashed potato incident, which Raw Story covered Thursday. This time she looked further back. When Donald was 2 and a half, she wrote, his mother "became very ill and was absent physically and emotionally for about a year." "He lost his connection to his primary caregiver at a crucial developmental stage, without any warning whatsoever," Mary Trump wrote. "His needs suddenly were not being met. His fears and longings went un-soothed." In her 2020 book, "Too Much and Never Enough," she wrote that her grandmother, Mary Anne MacLeod Trump, needed an emergency hysterectomy after complications from the birth of her youngest son, Robert, went undiagnosed. That left Donald with his father, Fred Trump Sr. Mary Trump says Fred looked like "a perfectly cheerful and very successful person" to outsiders but was "not affectionate, empathetic, or gentle" with his children, and was "incapable of comforting them." "During that year, Donald suffered deprivations that would scar him for life," she wrote. To cope with "those awful feelings of despair and terror," she argued, the toddler developed the traits the world would later see on full display: narcissism, bullying and grandiosity. "Unfortunately for him and the rest of the world, those were traits my grandfather actually admired and encouraged," she wrote. Fred Trump saw something in his second son, she wrote, either "a kindred spirit" or "someone who could be of use to him," and he "came to champion the very traits that would ultimately render Donald unlovable." At the same time, she wrote, young Donald was watching his father tear down her own father, Fred Trump Jr., the eldest son. Fred Sr. groomed him to inherit the family business by humiliating him whenever he fell short. Donald learned from it, according to the insider. Mary Trump wrote that he stopped acting as though he had any emotional needs at all, and that grievance, bullying and aggression took their place. She also described the rules of the house, which taught the Trump boys to be tough at all costs. Lying was fine. They were never to admit being wrong and never to apologize, "because kindness is weakness and admitting you are wrong is weakness." Fred believed "there can only be one winner and everybody else is a loser," she wrote. The result, she argued, is a man who has lost access to most of his own feelings. Fred "snuffed Freddy out," she wrote, but with Donald he "short circuited" his son's "ability to develop and experience the entire spectrum of human emotion." "With the exception of being around Vladimir Putin, have you ever seen Donald Trump smile in a genuine way?" she asked. "Have you ever seen him laugh uncontrollably? No. We see him angry. We see him bitter. We see him humiliated and defensive. On occasion, we see him smirking with contempt." She wrote that the pattern has only gotten worse with age. The more he senses that "the world sees him as a failure and a loser," the more he "overcompensates by being more corrupt, more cruel, more power mad." "Donald has turned himself into the monster my grandfather went out of his way to create," she wrote.
